front.title: What an Agent Audit Record Can and Cannot Establish

abstract.t: Agent audit records are signed, chained, counter-signed, timestamped, and registered with transparency services. Each mechanism establishes a narrower fact than it is often taken to establish. This document states, for any record format, protocol, or payment method, what a check of an agent audit record can and cannot establish about four properties: the independence of the entities that signed or observed it, the completeness of a set of records, the time at which a record or an action existed, and the result that a verifier reports. It defines independence by control rather than by key or process separation, separates the independence of a signer from the independence of an observation, states which commitments cannot support a report that a set of records is complete, and requires a verifier to report unauthenticated content as unauthenticated. It defines no record format, role, log, or service.
